title: Minstrel shows and his acrobat partner Harry Drew
summary: Carew describes minstrel show format and his friend Harry Drew, the acrobat.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: The minstrel show was a very popular thing at that time. And for a number of years after that, I don't know when it began to fade, maybe in the early twenties, I don't know, or the late, uh, 19s. But, uh, but, uh, at that time, minstrel shows were a big thing. And, uh, they, they, you've got some very good talent in minstrel shows. All good talent of all kinds. They didn't stand strictly on Negro stuff. But, uh, there were, there would be acrobatics and, uh, singers of other types there, you know, different acts, comedy acts and that. And of course, they had the, the ensemble at first, and they sat, uh, around the semicircle and cracked jokes and sang songs and all that. Then they broke up and, and afterwards they had the oleo, which was separate acts. After the intermission came the oleo of these different acts, which could be anything in the line of entertainment. But they were a very popular show and they had some very fine artists in those days. And, uh, I was always interested in shows that I said I thought I was going to become an acrobat myself. I got pretty good, if I do say so myself, but I never got into business that the boy I practiced with that was going to be my partner, he stuck to it and he became one of the best in the country. He was an acrobat for, oh, about 10 or 12 years. What was his name? Harry Drew, his name was. And he, he appeared with a number of acts, the Glyn Ceretti family, Alion Pizer, and, uh, oh, I don't know, quite a number of acts he appeared with and got into burlesque with, uh, along with it all, and lasted a number of years. But he never knew enough to get a good night's rest. He would, he would go through the show, do the show at night, then he'd go and play cards the rest of the night somewhere, and finally broke down his health. So he died out in, uh, California in the early 20s, about 1920 and 21, I believe it was. So, uh, did I say that there was always music around home, popular music, and...
